hints.title: Distance Bucket Partitioning
hints.text: Manhattan distance between workers and bikes is bounded by coordinates up to 1000, meaning distances span at most 2000. Group pairs into discrete distance buckets.

hints.title: Tie-Breaking Order
hints.text: When iterating across distances, visit smaller worker indices first, followed by smaller bike indices. This naturally satisfies the required tie-breaking criteria.

hints.title: Greedy Pairing Assignment
hints.text: Iterate from distance 0 to 2000. For each pair (w, b), if neither worker w nor bike b has been assigned, record the assignment and mark both as unavailable.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting N * M pairs with standard comparison sort takes O(N * M log(N * M)), which is slower than bucket sort.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bucket sort over bounded integer distances achieves linear O(N * M) performance.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize distance boundedness and use bucket sort to avoid general sorting overhead.
complexity.notes: Each worker and bike is assigned at most once.
